A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Explore-Then-Select work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching renamed components and relocated experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original VideoQA evaluations on Qwen2-VL and LLaVA-OneVision, alongside stage ablations, search-space analysis and timing measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, Qwen2.5-VL experiments, metric ablations and efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: Uniform frame selection, cosine-difference token selection, candidate construction and second-layer attention scoring remain unchanged. Static/dynamic frames are renamed key/delta frames; the expanded equations and explanations describe the same procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds MLVU long-video multiple-choice evaluation and ActivityNet-QA open-ended evaluation, retaining EgoSchema, VideoMME and MSVD-QA. These additions broaden the evaluated video collections and extend coverage to MLVU videos described as lasting up to two hours.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds reference comparisons with VideoChat2, LongVA, mPLUG-Owl3 and trained LongVU, explicitly acknowledging their limited comparability. Original, Retrieval, Similarity and reproduced LongVU accuracy comparisons remain. However, v1's direct runtime comparison against LongVU is removed.

E3.justification: New configurations include Qwen2.5-VL-7B evaluations and a sweep of 32–512 sampled frames with a fixed 32-frame budget in Table 6. Existing main experiments retain their sampling and budget settings. Table 7 lists Original at 256/128 sampled frames, so equivalence to the main tables' within-budget Original settings cannot be assumed.

E4.justification: Table 5 adds ablations testing query inclusion in attention keys and maximum versus mean aggregation. Table 6 replaces the brief timing comparison with a sampling-size analysis of accuracy, encoding cost and selection cost. The stage ablation extends to MLVU, while the existing qualitative and search-space analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2 newly states that reported timing measurements are averaged over 10 runs; v1 gives no repeat count. This adds run-reporting information without establishing an increase in runs. Neither version reports accuracy confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial benchmark, backbone, ablation and timing results, including 54.4% MLVU accuracy for Qwen2-VL at 256–64. Retained main benchmark scores match, but Figure 5 changes EgoSchema quarter/half search-space accuracies from 66.7/66.6 to 66.6/66.7. v1's 0.43-second versus 2.24-second LongVU timing comparison disappears; the new timings concern different experimental conditions.

T1.justification: v2 rewrites v1's top-token selection equation as an explicit difference score followed by index selection, preserving the same mathematical operation. Frame indexing, budget relationships and attention scoring remain equivalent. No new theorem, proof or substantive formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim training-free, query-adaptive allocation of static and dynamic information under limited token budgets, with plug-and-play applicability across models. The abstract and introduction retain the headline improvement of up to 5.8%; additional experiments support the existing central claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains smaller short-video gains through simpler scenes and coherent motion, and distinguishes increasing encoding cost from approximately stable selection cost. It also reframes the metric rationale around cumulative attention. Existing positional-encoding limitations and first-token latency qualifications remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code URL, specifies GPT-4o mini, discloses disabled generation sampling and an alternative 80GB A100 configuration, and documents the qualitative example's full search space. It also adds MLVU prompt/output details. Conversely, Appendix A.2 omits v1's explicit statement that reproduced LongVU uses top-K pruning to meet the budget.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for Qwen2.5-VL, MLVU, ActivityNet-QA, mPLUG-Owl3 and video GOP coding. The central positioning against KV-cache compression and training-dependent pre-input compression remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Substantial prose editing spans the abstract, related work, method exposition, experimental discussion and limitations. Frame terminology is standardized throughout, ablations are divided into stage and metric subsections, and the appendix is reorganized into additional experiments and prompt details.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn, and Figure 4 replaces displayed frames while retaining the same questions and token ratios. Tables gain benchmark columns and comparator blocks, with new metric, efficiency and Qwen2.5-VL tables. The original LongVU Table 4 moves to Appendix Table 9 and gains another model block.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in v1's validation: Table 5 tests previously unablated metric choices, Table 6 measures encoding as well as selection costs, and additional datasets and a third backbone better test generalization. Clearer exposition and the code URL improve reproducibility information. These substantial gains outweigh localized ambiguities concerning Table 7's Original frame budgets and the reproduced LongVU pruning procedure.
